name: Trattenbachtal & Trattenbachalm
kurzbeschreibung: The wild and romantic Trattenbachtal valley enchants with a fairytale waterfall, shady hiking trails, and an idyllic forest landscape.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Trattenbachtal unfolds as a romantic, largely untouched high-alpine side valley in the Kitzbühel Alps, branching south of Jochberg along the flanks of the Pass Thurn massif. Secluded from crowded tourist hubs and major lift installations, this tranquil mountain glen has meticulously preserved its authentic Tyrolean farming heritage and alpine serenity. Flowing through the valley is the torrential Trattenbach brook, which has carved deeply into slate bedrock over millenia, forging rushing waterfalls, sculpted stone pools, and cool forest gorges. Guarded by the green ridges and crags of the Zweitausender (2,004 m) and Kleiner Rettenstein (2,216 m), the valley enchants visitors with verdant pastures, alpine rose meadows, and fragrant spruce woodlands. The cultural heart of the glen is the historic, 300-year-old Trattenbachalm dairy chalet, situated at 1,540 meters elevation as a beacon of living mountain hospitality.

Route & Requirements

Hiking through the Trattenbachtal represents one of the most rewarding and peaceful half-day rambles for nature lovers and families in the Kitzbühel region. The standard trailhead begins off the Pass Thurn federal road at the Sauerkaser parking grounds. From there, a wide, moderately graded gravel forestry trail traces the rushing mountain torrent upstream (distance approx. 4.5 km to Trattenbachalm, 350 vertical meters ascent, walking time roughly 1.5 hours, easy grade T1/T2, suitable for all-terrain strollers). Along the way, a short signposted branch leads onto a timber viewing bridge over the roaring Trattenbach cataract. Energetic trekkers can continue beyond the pastures, ascending steep alpine singletrack via the upper meadows to the Zweitausender summit or across toward the Resterhöhe ridge (3.5 to 4 hours, 800 vertical meters gain, moderate grade T2). Sturdy hiking boots and weather-protective shells are advisable. Leashed dogs are permitted on all valley and pasture paths.

Visit & Arrival

Rail transit arrives via ÖBB trains into Kitzbühel main station. From the station, regional VVT bus 4010 departs toward Mittersill via Jochberg, stopping directly at the "Jochberg Wald / Sauerkaser" trailhead at the entrance of Trattenbachtal. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl-Ost) and follow highway B170 through Kitzbühel onto Pass Thurn road B161. Free hiker parking is situated right beside the turnoff into the valley. The valley is ideal for hiking from May through late October; the Trattenbachalm chalet welcomes guests from mid-June through early October.

Tips

Take a seat on the sun-bleached timber veranda of the historic Trattenbachalm to savor a traditional alpine wooden platter piled with cured farm bacon, sharp mountain cheese, and freshly baked crusty bread beneath the ramparts of Kleiner Rettenstein. On warm summer afternoons, dip your feet into the cool pebble pools of the Trattenbach stream.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Almbewirtschaftung Mitte Juni bis Anfang Oktober)
